A24's highly anticipated Peacock Crystal Lake series will screen its premiere episode at New York Comic Con a week before its official debut.

The Friday the 13th prequel series, Crystal Lake, will soon slash onto Peacock. To celebrate, the streamer has announced a Camp Crystal Lake experience taking place at New York Comic Con! And it looks like a bloody blast.

From October 8th-11th, fans at NYCC will be transported back to the 1970s at the seemingly idyllic Camp Crystal Lake—but will they survive their camp counsellor orientation?

The interactive experience is free for all New York Comic Con attendees and will deliver in-world thrills, Camp Crystal Lake photo moments, and branded giveaways.

Crystal Lake, the highly anticipated new horror series from A24 and creator, writer, executive producer and showrunner Brad Caleb Kane (It: Welcome to Derry) will drop all episodes on October 15th.

Expanding the iconic Friday the 13th horror movie universe, the eight-part series stars Emmy-winner Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees.

A prequel to the Friday the 13th franchise, Crystal Lake follows single mother Pam Voorhees (Linda Cardellini) who has been unable to shake her grief after her young, sickly son Jason Voorhees tragically drowned in the town lake almost a year before. When two strangers arrive at Pam's door digging into her past, a disturbing chain of events is set into motion, leaving the townspeople of Crystal Lake wondering: just who is Pam Voorhees?

Also starring Callum Vinson as young Jason Voorhees, William Catlett, Devin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins, and Gwendolyn Sundstrom, Crystal Lake expands the mythology of one of horror's most enduring franchises, blending psychological suspense, mystery and emotional storytelling with the legacy that has captivated audiences for generations.

Brad Caleb Kane joins A24 and original Friday the 13th writer Victor Miller and Horror, Inc. in bringing the Jason Universe story to the screen. Executive producers include Marc Toberoff, Victor Miller, Robert M. Barsamian, Robert P. Barsamian, Stuart Manashil, Tyson Bidner, Michael Lennox and Roy Lee. Produced by A24.

Each player is also given their own piece of undeveloped real estate along with a virtual toolbox with which to design and build anything — be it a navigable skyscraper, a working helicopter, a giant pinball machine, a multiplayer “Capture the Flag” game or some other, yet-to-be-dreamed-up creation. There is no cost for this first plot of virtual land. By participating and by building cool stuff, ROBLOX members can earn specialty badges as well as ROBLOX dollars (“Robux”). In turn, they can shop the online catalog to purchase avatar clothing and accessories as well as premium building materials, interactive components, and working mechanisms.
